title: SLA-aware compiler rollforward and fallback DSL
author: Elena Kim
content:
Summary:

This document defines a small domain-specific language (DSL) and operational playbook for doing SLA-aware rollforwards of compiler/kernel optimizations in the inference runtime, including automatic and operator-driven fallback behavior. The goal is to make compiler change rollouts predictable, observable, and reversible while protecting customer-facing SLOs (latency, availability, and cost).

Scope:
- Applies to changes that affect the serving runtime's compiled kernels or JIT passes: new kernel variants, quantization codegen tweaks, scheduling heuristics, and JIT flags that may affect latency distribution or token cost.
- Targets hosted and Dedicated runtimes; Private deployments should adopt the same DSL for compatibility but may change the enforcement policy per contract.

Why we need this:
- Small compiler changes can change tail latency or token efficiency in subtle ways (e.g., a kernel that reduces average cost but regresses p99).
- Operators must be able to stage, verify, and automatically rollback changes when SLOs are violated.
- We need a repeatable, machine-readable specification to run canaries and safe rollouts across regions and capacity tiers.

Definitions:
- Rollforward: a deployment of a compiler/kernelset version to production pools.
- Canary cohort: subset of traffic or tenants selected for preflight verification.
- Safety signal: a measured metric (SLO/SLI) that, when breached, triggers automatic fallback.
- Fallback: reverting to a compatible kernelset or model-variant that restores the safety signal.

DSL overview (examples and semantics):
- Purpose: declare target kernelset, cohorts, SLO guards, and fallback policy in one JSON/YAML document consumed by the rollout controller.
- Required fields: id, kernelset, cohorts, metrics, thresholds, evaluation_window, fallback_policy, owner, preflight_checks.

Example (YAML-like but the controller accepts JSON):

---
id: cf-roll-2026-03
kernelset: compiler-v2.4-jit-agg
cohorts:
  - name: canary-small
    tenant_selector: {percent: 0.5}    # 0.5% of total requests across canary regions
    regions: [us-west1, eu-west1]
  - name: progressive
    tenant_selector: {percent: 10}     # next 10% if canary passes
metrics:
  - name: p99_inference_latency_ms
    source: metrics.request_latency.p99
    direction: "<="
    target: "350"                 # milliseconds
  - name: error_rate
    source: metrics.request_errors.rate_1m
    direction: "<="
    target: "0.002"               # 0.2% errors
  - name: token_cost_per_1k
    source: metrics.token_cost.rolling_5m
    direction: "<="
    target: "1.50"                # dollars per 1k tokens
evaluation_window: "5m"
preflight_checks:
  - name: perf-smoke
    runbook: perf-smoke-suite --target canary-small --duration 3m
  - name: correctness-sanity
    runbook: evaller run --promptset basic-consistency --cohort canary-small
fallback_policy:
  mode: automatic
  threshold_tolerance: 1
  revert_to: compiler-v2.3
  cool_down: "15m"
  escalation: |
    If automatic fallback fires twice within 24h, create urgent incident and notify SRE/Compiler teams.
owner: runtime-compiler@redwood.com
---

Rollout phases and algorithm:
1. PREPARE: Create rollout spec and run preflight_checks in staging and canary lab. Verify test harness results and attach artifacts (profiles, flamegraphs).
2. CANARY: Deploy to canary-small cohort (0.5% traffic). Monitor evaluation_window signals continuously.
3. PROGRESSIVE: If canary passes for 3 consecutive evaluation windows, expand to progressive cohort.
4. RAMP: Gradual expansion in steps (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), each step requires X consecutive good windows (configurable).
5. STABILIZE: Maintain full rollout for stabilization window (30–60 minutes) before marking rollout complete.

Safety invariants (hard requirements enforced by the rollout controller):
- The rollout controller will not expand cohorts if any metric listed in metrics breaches its target in the last evaluation_window.
- Automatic fallback triggers if breach persists for 2 consecutive windows (configurable per rollout).
- Fallback must not cause oscillation: controller applies cool_down after a revert before allowing a new rollout to same kernelset.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Core telemetry signals (metrics.*) the controller consumes: request_latency.p50/p95/p99, request_errors.rate_1m, token_cost.rolling_5m, kv_cache.hit_rate, gpu_util.percentile_95, p95_cpu_ms_per_token.
- Suggested dashboard panels (Grafana):
  - Rollout summary: active rollout id, current cohort, percent of traffic, last evaluation result.
  - Safety panel: per-region p99, error rate, token cost, and a colored status (green/yellow/red) computed using thresholds.
  - Comparison heatmap: difference between new and baseline kernelset for each metric (delta and ratio).
  - Canary flamegraphs: callsite-level hotpaths for canary vs baseline to aid triage.

Prometheus alert rules (recommended examples):
ALERT Rollout_P99_Regression
IF increase(metrics.request_latency.p99{kernelset=~".*"}[5m]) > 50 and metrics.request_latency.p99{kernelset="candidate"} > 350
FOR 10m
LABELS {severity="page"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary="Candidate kernelset p99 increased > 50ms and exceeded 350ms for 10m"}

Operational runbook (fast path for operator when a rollout degrades):
1) Detect: Pager/alert triggers Rollout_P99_Regression or Rollout_Error_Rate_High.
2) Inspect rollout controller UI: note rollout id, current cohort, and last two evaluation windows.
3) Run quick diagnostics:
   - Verify topology: curl internal health endpoints /healthz for runtime-compiler and inference-router in affected regions.
   - Compare metrics: kubectl port-forward prometheus 9090 && promql 'metrics.request_latency.p99{kernelset="candidate"} - metrics.request_latency.p99{kernelset="baseline"}'
   - Fetch canary flamegraphs: s3://perf-artifacts/{rollout_id}/canary/*
4) If automatic fallback has not already fired, use controller action: Revert -> executes revert_to and triggers cool_down. Document reason and attach traces.
5) If revert fails or oscillation is detected, escalate to on-call compiler engineer and SRE: tag incident with "compiler-rollforward" and run full rollback checklist.
6) Post-incident: capture root cause, add new perf tests, and update the rollout spec with additional preflight checks.

Canary test matrix (minimum):
- Traffic profile: short-chat (avg tokens/request 20), long-context (avg 1k tokens), embeddings (batch inference).
- Load levels: 10% baseline load, 50% baseline load, and transient 2x bursts for 30s.
- Hardware coverage: GPU types in target regions (A100, H100, L40).
- KV-cache states: warm, cold, partially-warm.

Preflight automation checklist (what CI must run before controller accepts spec):
- Unit & integration tests for compiler changes (green).
- Perf smoke suite over representative sample (p95 within 5% of baseline).
- Deterministic correctness tests: model-output consistency checks on 1k prompts.
- Artifact upload: kernel binary, compile flags, hash, and provenance metadata.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Runtime Compiler Team: authors the kernelset, writes perf profiles, and owns canary diagnostics.
- Eng Platform (Rollout Controller): validates spec syntactically, enforces safety invariants, and executes cohorts.
- SRE Oncall: primary responder for production degradations, triggers rollback if automatic fallback fails or if operator judgment deems necessary.
- Observability Team: maintains dashboards and alerts used by the controller.

Post-deployment retrospective requirements (for any rollout that invoked fallback or produced >10% SLO burn):
- Owner must file a one-page postmortem: summary, timeline, root cause, remediation, and updated preflight checks.
- Add a targeted synthetic test to the perf-smoke-suite covering the failing scenario.

Versioning and audit trail:
- Every rollout spec is immutable once submitted: mutations produce a new rollout id.
- The controller logs events to auditing-service with fields: rollout_id, event_type, actor, timestamp, reason, metrics_snapshot_url.

Developer tips and common failure modes:
- Small changes to memory layout can increase p99 due to worse cache locality even if average improves. Always check p95/p99 separately.
- Quantization tweaks sometimes increase generation drift on rare prompts: include random prompt sampling in correctness-sanity.
- GPU kernel scheduling changes may interact with tenant fair-share; validate tenant isolation scenarios during canary.

Appendices:
A) Quick CLI examples:
- Create rollout: rfcctl apply -f rollout-spec.json --dry-run=false
- Check status: rfcctl status cf-roll-2026-03 --output yaml
- Force revert: rfcctl revert cf-roll-2026-03 --reason "manual revert after p99 regression"

B) Minimal JSON schema (controller consumer) excerpt:
{
  "id": "string",
  "kernelset": "string",
  "cohorts": [ { "name": "string", "tenant_selector": {"percent": number}, "regions": ["string"] } ],
  "metrics": [ { "name": "string", "source": "string", "direction": "<=|>=", "target": "string" } ],
  "evaluation_window": "string",
  "fallback_policy": { "mode": "automatic|manual", "revert_to": "string", "cool_down": "string" }
}
C) Related documentation: runtime compiler design doc, rollout controller API reference, perf-smoke-suite repository.
